title: Operator Readiness: Smoke Tests & Ops Simulations
author: Priya Banerjee
content:
Overview:
This document defines a standardized program for operator readiness driven by automated smoke tests and scheduled operations simulations (ops-sims). The program's goal is to reduce time-to-detect, improve first-response accuracy, and validate runbook/automation effectiveness before customer impact. It complements regular game-days by focusing on repeatable, measurable smoke-test workflows that run as part of CI and during oncall rotations.

Scope:
- Services: inference-api, routing-service, kv-cache, model-proxy, quota-gateway
- Operators: first-responder oncall, SRE bridge, service owner, customer success liaison (for customer-facing scenarios)
- Test types: fast smoke (30s–5m), stability smoke (5m–30m), degraded-path simulation (15m–2h)

Why this matters:
1) Catch regressions in alarm-to-remediation flows before production impact.
2) Ensure runbooks are executable by new responders.
3) Validate automation (auto-scaling, fallback routing, cache warming) under realistic load patterns.
4) Produce reproducible evidence for post-incident retros and regulatory audits.

Program Components:
1) Smoke-test harness and CI integration
   - A small Go-based test runner (cmd/smoke-runner) executes scenario scripts against test and staging clusters and publishes results to the Operator Dashboard.
   - CI jobs: smoke-fast (on PR to infra/runtime), smoke-nightly (staging), smoke-full-weekly (multi-region)
   - Failure policy: failing smoke-fast blocks merges to main for changes touching runtime infra.

2) Ops-sim calendar and cadence
   - Mini-sims: 1-hour focused sims run weekly per service team (first-responder + owner).
   - Full-sims: 4-hour cross-functional sims (SRE, runtime, customer success, product) run quarterly and are scored.
   - Post-sim retro and action tracking mandatory within 72 hours.

3) Runbook validation matrix
   - Every critical runbook is assigned a verification frequency: smoke (weekly), quarterly sim (quarterly), code-coupled test (on PR).
   - Owners maintain a checklist in the runbook header indicating last-verified date and verifier.

Minimum Acceptance Criteria (table):
| Item | Threshold | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|
| Alert generation latency | <= 60s from fault injection | Alert ID + timestamp in Operator Dashboard |
| First ack time (sim) | <= 5 min | Pager event + oncall ack log |
| Runbook reproducibility | 90% steps succeed in staging | Step-level pass/fail artifacts (logs/screenshots) |
| Automated fallback success | 95% for injected failure mode | Traffic routing logs, request success % |

Triggering smoke tests (how-to):
1) Via CI: push to repo that contains change to runtime/core triggers smoke-fast.
2) Manual run: use smoke-runner CLI per section below for ad-hoc validation during oncall handoff.

Smoke-runner CLI examples:
- Quick check (fast smoke): 
  ./smoke-runner --scenario basic-echo --target staging --timeout 60s
- Degraded-path sim (full): 
  ./smoke-runner --scenario kv-eviction-and-slow-proxy --target staging --duration 20m --collect-traces

Sample smoke scenario (YAML):
---
name: kv-eviction-and-slow-proxy
steps:
  - id: priming-traffic
    type: traffic
    qps: 20
    duration: 60s
    assertion: 99th_p99_latency < 200ms
  - id: evict-kv
    type: fault-inject
    service: kv-cache
    action: evict-keys
    keys: sample-key-prefix*
  - id: slow-proxy
    type: fault-inject
    service: model-proxy
    action: add-latency
    milliseconds: 300
  - id: validate-fallback
    type: assertion
    query: /healthz?route=fallback
    expected_status: 200
---
(Place scenario files in repo: infra/op-sims/scenarios/)

Escalation & Communication Flow (numbered run):
1) Detect: Monitoring fires alerts into PagerDuty, with tags: service, region, impact-lanes.
2) Acknowledge: First-responder acknowledges in <5 min, posts short status in Slack #ops-bridge and creates a sim ticket if running test.
3) Assess: Triage & impact classification by owner using the Decision Ladder (see below).
4) Execute: Follow validated runbook steps; invoke automation where safe.
5) Bridge: If >30 minutes without resolution or cross-service impacts, open a bridge and invite SRE and CS.
6) Customer Notice: For customer-affecting incidents, use the Customer Comms Template below within 60 minutes of bridge formation.

Decision Ladder (triage rubric):
- Step 1: Is the alert actionable? (yes -> proceed, no -> adjust alert)
- Step 2: Scope: single-tenant, multi-tenant, whole-region
- Step 3: Severity: S1 (outage), S2 (degraded), S3 (no customer impact)
- Step 4: Containment strategy: throttle, fallback, rollback, capacity add

Customer Comms Templates (short and long):
- Short status (initial, internal copy to CS):
  Subject: Redwood inference — Investigating elevated latency in <region>
  Body: We are investigating reports of increased latency affecting inference requests in <region>. We have opened a bridge and are working to identify the root cause. We will provide updates every 30 minutes. Impacted customers: <list>.

- Public status page template (for StatusPage):
  Title: Degraded inference latency — <region>
  Summary: We are currently experiencing elevated latency for inference requests in <region>. Traffic is being routed to fallback hosts where possible.
  Latest update: <time> — Engineers have identified a cache eviction pattern and are running mitigations.

Ops-sim Scoring Rubric (full-sim):
- Detection score (30 pts): alerts produced and routed correctly (0–30).
- Response score (30 pts): ack time, runbook execution completeness (0–30).
- Communication score (20 pts): bridge establishment, customer notice cadence (0–20).
- Remediation score (20 pts): solution correctness, post-sim artifact quality (0–20).
A passing sim requires >= 75 total points and no critical gaps in runbook steps.

Post-sim Retro Template (actionable):
1) Summary of scenario and timeline (who, what, when).
2) Findings (what worked, what failed).
3) Actions (owner, due date, validation step).
4) Evidence (logs, CI smoke link, runbook version).
5) Policy changes (alert tuning, runbook edits).

Ownership matrix (table):
| Role | Primary responsibilities | On-sim expectation |
|---|---|---:|
| First-responder | Ack, initial triage, runbook start | Execute first two runbook blocks |
| Service owner | Deep troubleshooting, code rollbacks | Lead root cause analysis |
| SRE bridge | Bridge coordination, cross-service calls | Maintain timeline + status page updates |
| Customer Success | Customer notices, FAQs | Draft public messaging and CS Q&A |

Runbook Quality Checklist (to be in every runbook header):
- [ ] Has a clear owner and last-verified date
- [ ] Steps are executable by a non-owner operator
- [ ] Includes safe-rollback instructions and automation guardrails
- [ ] Contains smoke-test scenario name and repo path
- [ ] Links to related dashboards and traces

Operational SOPs (short):
- Oncall handoff: outgoing oncall runs smoke-fast against staging with scenario: handoff-sanity within 15 minutes of the handoff window and attaches result to handoff note.
- New runbook onboarding: new runbooks must pass a first verification smoke within 7 days of creation.
- Runbook pruning: owners should remove/annotate steps that are no longer valid during quarterly review.

Evidence retention and compliance:
- Smoke-test logs retained for 90 days in logstore.
- Full sim artifacts (videos of bridge, timing spreadsheets, scored rubric) retained for 12 months in the retro archive.
- Regulated-customer scenarios tagged and stored separately with restricted access.

Appendix A — Example Post-sim Action (realistic):
- Action: Add a cache-warming preflight when restarting proxy pods
- Owner: Marcus Chen
- Due: 2025-07-01
- Validation: smoke-runner scenario kv-eviction-and-slow-proxy passes in staging with fallback success >95%
